skill.name: Set image width and height attributes for aspect ratio inference
skill.description: Canonical skill for declaring image dimensions in HTML to enable browser aspect-ratio inference and prevent cumulative layout shift. Applies to static images with known aspect ratios.
skill.skill_body: Modern browsers automatically infer the aspect ratio of an image from its width and height attributes. By setting both width and height on img elements, the browser can reserve sufficient space before the image loads, preventing text and other content from shifting down the page. This is the modern best practice for preventing layout shifts caused by late-loading images. ## Objective layout_shift_prevention_reference ## Applicable Signals - Developer or designer needs to understand modern best practice for declaring image dimensions in HTML - Layout shift issues are being investigated and root cause analysis points to unspecified image dimensions - New image markup is being created or reviewed ## Contraindications - Image dimensions are dynamically generated or truly variable with no static aspect ratio available - Image is responsive and dimensions change based on viewport or container width ## Workflow Steps - {'step': 1, 'action': "Identify the image's aspect ratio", 'detail': 'Determine the ratio of width to height (e.g., 16:9, 4:3). If one dimension is known, calculate the other using the aspect ratio formula.'} - {'step': 2, 'action': 'Set width and height attributes on the img element', 'detail': "Add both width and height attributes to the img tag with values that match the image's actual aspect ratio."} - {'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify browser behavior', 'detail': 'Modern browsers will automatically add a default aspect ratio based on the width and height attributes, reserving space before the image loads.'} ## Constraints - Both width and height attributes must be present on the img element - The width and height values must reflect the actual aspect ratio of the image ## Cautions - Setting incorrect width and height values will distort the image or reserve wrong space - This approach works for static images; responsive images require additional CSS techniques ## Output Contract - Developer understands that setting width and height attributes on img elements allows modern browsers to infer aspect ratio and reserve space automatically, preventing layout shifts during image load ## Example Therapist Responses ### Example 1 - Client/Input: Image file puppy.jpg with 640px width and 360px height (16:9 aspect ratio) - Therapist/Output: - Notes: Browser reserves 640×360px space before image loads, preventing text shift ### Example 2 - Client/Input: Image with known height of 360px and 16:9 aspect ratio - Therapist/Output: Width = 360 × (16 / 9) = 640px; set width="640" height="360" - Notes: Aspect ratio allows calculation of missing dimension
